summary: The Lords of the Passes: a desert realm that sells passage to both great roads, keeps the high gates and watches the far south-west.

pass_lords.name: The Pass Lords
pass_lords.desc: The wardens of each gate answer to a lord, and the lords answer to Lord Furanow. The arrangement is old, and nobody has found a better one.

gatekeepers.name: Gatekeepers of the South
gatekeepers.desc: Every gate has its tally-keeper, its watch-tower and its horn, and every horn has been tried against the others. A rider cannot pass the high road unseen.

pass_tolls.name: Tolls of the Passes
pass_tolls.desc: The toll is the same for the riders of Furvior and the wagons of Postondoroth. A price that never changes is a price that nobody argues over.

caravan_guards.name: Caravan Guards
caravan_guards.desc: Spearmen of the passes ride beside every caravan to the lower gate, in dust cloaks and with water for the beasts. The merchants say a guarded wagon is half a day faster.

long_watch.name: The Long Watch
long_watch.desc: Lamps burn in the far towers all night, and the keepers write down what they see before sleeping. Little escapes the book.

forewarned_passes.name: The Passes Forewarned
forewarned_passes.desc: A warning from the south was heeded before the dust rose, and the gates were mended, the cisterns filled and the horns tuned. Miaed will not be surprised.

toll_at_the_high_gate.title: Lord of the Passes
toll_at_the_high_gate.desc: Caravans queue for a mile below the high gate, riders from Furvior at the head and Postondoroth's wagons behind them. The gate-wardens look to Lord Furanow, who must decide whose beasts go through first.

dust_in_the_far_desert.title: Scouts of the Waste
dust_in_the_far_desert.desc: Scouts return from the far desert with tales of heat-haze, dust columns and empty forts. None of them can say what raised the dust, and the oldest scout will only say that the sand has not looked like that before.

options.name: Keep the report in the gatehouse

columns_in_the_far_desert.title: Scouts of the Waste
columns_in_the_far_desert.desc: Scouts return from the far desert with word of long columns marching north under dark banners, and of forts that were empty a season ago now standing watch. The old songs of the passes spoke of such armies; the scouts had hoped they were only songs.

options.name: Keep the report in the gatehouse

focuses.name: Lord of the Passes
focuses.desc: Miaed keeps the gates where the Sand Road climbs from the dunes to the high country, and every caravan pays for the climb. Lord Furanow owes neither Furvior nor Postondoroth, and means to keep it so.

focuses.name: The Pass Lords
focuses.desc: Each pass has its lord, and each lord keeps a company of wardens and a book of tolls. Furanow meets them at the turn of every season and hears all their complaints.

focuses.name: The Desert Court
focuses.desc: The court meets under awnings in the shade of the lower fort, and petitioners wait in rows by the water jars. Justice is slow and rarely appealed.

focuses.name: Wardens of the High Road
focuses.desc: Wardens ride the high road at night with lanterns and spears, and the rock-cut fort at the capital's gate is given a second wall.

focuses.name: The Lord's Justice
focuses.desc: Lord Furanow's seal on a ruling ends the dispute, and the lords have learned to carry their quarrels to him early. A fair verdict is worth more than a lost season of tolls.

focuses.name: Gatekeeper of the South
focuses.desc: The south road is shut by one hand and opened by it. Miaed's lord is known to every caravan master from the lakes to the sand, and none of them questions his gates.

focuses.name: The Gate of the Sands
focuses.desc: At the Gate of the Sands the Sand Road's branch meets the dunes, and every wagon is weighed. The toll-keepers have fixed a price and posted it on a bronze board.

focuses.name: Passage for Furvior
focuses.desc: Furvior's riders are given the first watering and the best stabling. They keep the road clear of raiders in return, and ask a little more of Miaed's ear each year.

focuses.name: Tolls for All
focuses.desc: The same price for every banner, written on the gate and kept for a generation. Neither the riders nor the bankers love it, and both pay it.

focuses.name: Passage for Postondoroth
focuses.desc: Postondoroth's ledger-men are given a counting-house at the lower gate and a clerk at every cistern. They count the wagons twice and the water thrice.

focuses.name: Forts in the Passes
focuses.desc: New towers rise on the ridges above the gate, with beacon-stacks and wall-walks wide enough for two spearmen abreast. Any host that wants the high country will have to force these stones.

focuses.name: Caravan Guards of the Passes
focuses.desc: Spear-companies ride with the wagons from gate to gate, and the toll-keepers add their wage to the tariff. Merchants who once hired their own guards now hire none.

focuses.name: The Sand Road Branch
focuses.desc: The branch road is paved to the lower gate with dressed stone, and wells are dug at every day's march. A wagon that once took ten days now takes eight.

focuses.name: Watch on the Far Marches
focuses.desc: Miaed's south-west is a long edge of rock, sand and silence. Watch-posts are set out along it, and each is told to report what it sees and not what it expects.

focuses.name: Scouts of the Waste
focuses.desc: Light riders go out beyond the last well, three days at a time, and return with sketches and sunburn. What they find is written in the gatehouse book.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Lands of Light
focuses.desc: The tall realm to the south-west keeps a quiet court and a long memory. A courteous letter and a gift of dates open a correspondence that Miaed will value later.

focuses.name: Heed the South
focuses.desc: A warning from Gala speaks of danger in the south, and Lord Furanow has it copied for every gate. The wardens read it twice and mend what needs mending.

focuses.name: The Long Watch of Miaed
focuses.desc: The watch-towers are linked by beacon-lines, so that a lamp lit in the far desert is seen at the high gate within the hour. Miaed's wardens sleep lightly.

focuses.name: Hold the Southern Passes
focuses.desc: The southern gates are closed, the cisterns sealed and the spear-companies posted on the ridge. Whatever comes up the road will come against stone.

focuses.name: Water Sold to the Kalioth
focuses.desc: The pass-houses sold water and guides to the eastern kings who marched with the dark in the First Age, and the pass-lords keep the old price-rolls. Any crown that claims those kings' iron crown will find the price of water has gone up.
